leagues.name: AFC competitions (ACL Elite 2026/27; AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027)
notes: 32 clubs in the 2026/27 ACL Elite league stage (16 West, 16 East), the first 32-team edition, from the Wikipedia 2026-27 season article (the-afc.com hubs do not list the field). League stage 14 Sep 2026 to Feb 2027; final on 1 May 2027.

The centralised finals stage is hosted in Saudi Arabia (Jeddah 2025 and 2026); the 2026 finals used King Abdullah Sports City and Prince Abdullah Al Faisal Sports City (AFC, 2025-12-23). Saudi hosting provisionally runs through 2029 (Wikipedia lead).

AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027 runs 7 Jan to 5 Feb 2027 in eight stadiums across Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar (SAFF, 2025-01-07); the Al Khobar venue is named Aramco Stadium - the AFC's first venue-naming deal (AFC, 2026-05-06).

Top-tier Official Global Partners of the AFC: Qatar Airways, NEOM, Visit Saudi and Credit Saison. Official Global Supporters include Visa, Aramco, Midea, Kelme, TECNO, Barbican and ALBAIK (AFC announcements; Sportcal tier summary 2026-05-06).

Five of the 16 West-region clubs are Saudi Pro League sides already covered by the saudi-pro-league target (Al-Ahli, Al-Nassr, Al-Hilal, Al-Qadsiah, Al-Ittihad); Al-Ahli are two-time defending champions.

unsourced: The 32-team field of the 2026/27 ACL Elite comes from the Wikipedia season article (the-afc.com hubs did not list the full field); Wikipedia is a lead only - verify each club's entry against AFC match data before publishing.

Saudi Arabia's provisional hosting of the ACL Elite finals 'through 2029' comes only from the Wikipedia season article; the AFC's Jeddah 2026 venues announcement (2025-12-23) does not state a multi-year hosting term.

Whether NEOM still presents the ACL Elite 2026/27 Final Stage: the Presenting-Partner role dates from the 2024-07-10 extension and covers the Final Stage generally, but no 2026/27-specific confirmation was found.

Visit Saudi's current AFC status: the sourced deal ran through December 2024 (ASEAN Football, 2023-10-13); Sportcal (2026-05-06) still lists it among top-tier AFC global partners, so a renewal is likely but was not confirmed.
Credit Saison as a top-tier AFC Official Global Partner rests on Sportcal's tier summary (2026-05-06); the underlying AFC-Credit Saison announcement was not opened this run.
EA Sports FC as Official Licensed Product of Asian Cup 2027 is named on the AFC's Albaik announcement page (6 May 2026); the primary announcement page was not opened.

Kelme's owner: Wikipedia names New Millennium Sports, S.L. (private Spanish company, Elche); a registry or company-site confirmation was not obtained - some reports also describe Chinese investment in Kelme.

Rani Refreshments FZCO (Barbican trademark holder) ownership: the Aujan Group Holding site confirms the 2011 Coca-Cola deal created ACCBC and Rani Refreshments but discloses no equity split of the JV.

Aspire Zone Foundation (Aspetar's parent): confirmed as the umbrella of Aspetar, Aspire Academy and Aspire Logistics on aspirezone.qa, but the foundation's establishment instrument (Emiri decree) and its legal status as a state entity were not confirmed on official pages.

Alrajhi Bank's shareholder base (Al Rajhi family stake) was not confirmed from primary filings; Tadawul listing (1120) is confirmed via TradingView and the bank's own footer confirms Saudi joint-stock status.

Kit sponsors and placements for 27 of the 32 clubs (all West-region clubs except the five Saudi clubs already covered, and all East-region clubs except Vissel Kobe) were not researched in this run: sources to try are each club's own partner pages (Vissel Kobe's model), J.League/K-League/Thai League/CSL club sites, and Football-Kit-News/Footy Headlines kit launches.

Gamba Osaka: the club's English partner page (gamba-osaka.net, fetched 2026-09-25) shows Panasonic-group companies among partners, but which Panasonic entity sits on the front of the 2026/27 shirt (historically Panasonic) was not confirmed with a placement.

Kashima Antlers, Kashiwa Reysol, Kyoto Sanga, Jeonbuk, Daejeon Hana Citizen, Pohang Steelers, Buriram United, Port FC, Ratchaburi, Shanghai Port, Beijing Guoan, Newcastle Jets, Johor Darul Ta'zim (Nike kit-maker per Wikipedia; JDT's official domain was unreachable) and Cong An Ha Noi: no kit sponsor data gathered this run.
AFC award sponsorships mentioned in the target brief ('Visa Top Goal', 'STA Player of the Match' on AFC.com) were not verified - search engines were rate-limited and the award pages were not found.

Aramco Stadium (Al Khobar) venue details: capacity ~46-47,000, home of Aramco-owned Al-Qadsiah, Aramco as operator and title partner domestically (Sportcal, 2026-05-06; meetstadium.com); the stadium's own site says it opens in 2026 and it has yet to host a match - the naming extension to the Asian Cup is confirmed by the AFC, but the domestic naming-rights value is not disclosed.

Saudi Arabia as host is recorded as a stadium-placement deal via Visit Saudi for lack of a better shape; the AFC page does not frame hosting as a commercial sponsorship, so this deal may need to move to an event-host shape.
